trickyParts: kvwatch keeps one complete flag (the atomic) that both #2167's Complete() and the resume read; a resumed generation is complete at its own nil marker, and a WithRescan rescan passes no connection so it always reads in full.
A full-read generation resets hw to 0, so an hw above LastSeq (a restored older snapshot) cannot force a full read at every later Rewatch.

The reaper deletes with nats.LastRevision(checked revision); JetStream's wrong-last-sequence answer (nats.ErrKeyExists) counts as skipped. Revision 0 falls back to deleteInterest because LastRevision(0) is no condition.
The session cache does not insert an already-expired put for an id it does not hold, so a stale delivery after the fence has gone cannot make the id live or bring back a LastSeen answer.
EV-11 lives in Registry.UpsertWithin (#2167), which Upsert and the subscribe route both reach.
deviations: The race job: #2167 added a listener race step, so ./internal/session/ joined that step (plan T5's stated alternative); kvwatch was already in it.
#2167's TestCompleteIsTheCurrentWatchersFirstScanDeliveringEveryKey now writes a key while its watcher is away, because a rewatch resumes and delivers nothing otherwise; it checks the same thing.
Before/after numbers are main ae36683e (merge base after #2167 and INFRA-610) against the head; the earlier 1357b95c run is kept in the artifact and agrees.
The restart test asserts resumed with 0 entries: the server is down during the restart, so no write lands while the listener is away; the k-writes case is resume_test.go's.
openQuestions: R7's gate is the tester's: INFRA-610's production check showing all three listeners on its build before this goes to review.
